@graph.name: LibreCourseUY
@graph.description: Join a non-profit FOSS community from Uruguay. Discover projects, learn together and make your first open source contribution.

acceptedAnswer.text: A non-profit initiative based in Uruguay that helps programmers, from aspiring developers to seasoned professionals, contribute to Free and Open Source Software.
Anyone, for free. Members are expected to follow our Code of Conduct. Contributions follow the license and contribution terms of each project.
A strong developer community with common goals, a space to learn and grow your career, and real projects worth putting on your CV.

Follow our first contribution guide : choose a project, find a small task and prepare your tools. If you need help choosing, ask in Discord . Our learning guide explains how to learn through real projects with community support.

mainEntity.name: Where can I see recent project activity?

acceptedAnswer.text: Visit Gitsion to follow updates by project or contributor, browse issues and see pull requests. Our project directory helps you discover projects by category, language and contribution status.

Open source is a global conversation, and English is its common language. Writing issues, PRs, and documentation in English makes your contributions accessible to the entire FOSS community, not just Spanish speakers. It also prepares you for real-world collaboration on any project, anywhere.
Contribute on GitHub Join on our Discord server Follow us on Instagram and LinkedIn Talk on Reddit: r/LibreCourseUY , r/VibeCodingUY and r/ClaudeCodeUY Chat on IRC: #LibreCourseUY on irc.libera.chat

LibreCourseUY is a volunteer-run, non-profit community with no formal hierarchy. Carlos A. Planchón and Emiliano Gandini coordinate it and make the final decisions. See how we are organized on the About page.

Project owners retain ownership and governance of their work. Contributions follow each project's license and contribution terms. LibreCourseUY does not claim rights over members' private projects or proprietary code.

mainEntity.name: Can I bring a private or commercial project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can bring projects with private or commercial components. Collaboration organized through LibreCourseUY must happen on the open source parts of those projects. The private part remains yours. Commercial or proprietary work, including paid development, employment, consulting, equity arrangements or work under NDA, must be agreed independently between the members involved. LibreCourseUY is not a party to those agreements.
